concepts.name: Synchronous versus asynchronous execution
concepts.summary: Explain that synchronous code runs line by line and blocks, while asynchronous work is started now and finishes later without halting other code.

concepts.name: Single-threaded execution model
concepts.summary: Understand that JavaScript runs one piece of code at a time on a single main thread, so long tasks freeze the page.

concepts.name: Callback functions
concepts.summary: Describe a callback as a function passed to another function to be called later, when work completes.

concepts.name: Timers with setTimeout
concepts.summary: Recall how setTimeout and setInterval schedule a function to run after a delay and how clearTimeout cancels it.

concepts.name: Common asynchronous sources
concepts.summary: Recognise typical asynchronous operations such as network requests, timers, file access and user events.

concepts.name: Promise states and meaning
concepts.summary: Explain that a promise represents a future value and is pending, then either fulfilled with a value or rejected with a reason.

misconceptions.text: setTimeout with a delay of 0 runs the function immediately, before the next line of code.
Asynchronous code runs at the same time as other JavaScript code on separate threads.
A line of code after an asynchronous call will wait until that call has finished.

concepts.name: Consuming promises with then and catch
concepts.summary: Use then, catch and finally to handle the result, error and cleanup of a promise.

concepts.name: Promise chaining
concepts.summary: Chain then calls, returning values or promises, so that each step receives the previous step's result.

concepts.name: Async and await syntax
concepts.summary: Write async functions that use await to pause until a promise settles and always return a promise.

concepts.name: Fetching data with fetch
concepts.summary: Request data using fetch and parse the response body with json(), handling its promise-based steps.

concepts.name: Error handling with try/catch
concepts.summary: Wrap awaited calls in try/catch to handle rejections and failed requests.

concepts.name: Callback error-first convention
concepts.summary: Read and write callbacks whose first argument carries an error, and handle it before using the result.

concepts.name: Creating promises with constructor
concepts.summary: Wrap a callback-based operation in new Promise, calling resolve or reject appropriately.

misconceptions.text: fetch rejects its promise when the server responds with an HTTP error such as 404 or 500.
Using await makes the whole program stop and wait, blocking the main thread.
A then handler's return value is ignored, so there is no need to return a promise inside a chain.

concepts.name: Event loop, call stack and queues
concepts.summary: Analyse how the call stack, Web APIs and task queue interact to decide when callbacks run.

concepts.name: Microtasks versus macrotasks
concepts.summary: Predict the output order of code mixing promise callbacks, timers and synchronous statements.

concepts.name: Parallel execution with Promise.all
concepts.summary: Start independent tasks together and await them with Promise.all, understanding its fail-fast behaviour.

concepts.name: Promise combinators
concepts.summary: Choose among all, allSettled, race and any based on how results and failures should be combined.

concepts.name: Sequential versus parallel awaiting
concepts.summary: Analyse when awaiting in a loop serialises work needlessly and restructure it for appropriate concurrency.

concepts.name: Error propagation through chains
concepts.summary: Trace how errors and rejections travel through chains and async functions and where they must be caught.

concepts.name: Cancellation with AbortController
concepts.summary: Cancel fetch requests and implement timeouts using an AbortController signal.

misconceptions.text: Promise.all runs the promises in parallel on multiple threads.
A setTimeout callback with zero delay runs before an already resolved promise's then callback.
Promise.all waits for every promise and returns partial results even if one rejects.

concepts.name: Concurrency limiting and pooling
concepts.summary: Evaluate and implement limits on simultaneous asynchronous tasks to avoid overloading servers or resources.

concepts.name: Retry with backoff
concepts.summary: Judge which failures merit retries and design retry strategies with delays and caps.

concepts.name: Race conditions in async code
concepts.summary: Identify how interleaved async operations produce out-of-order results or shared-state bugs and guard against them.

concepts.name: Async iteration and generators
concepts.summary: Consume and produce sequences of asynchronous values using for await...of and async generators.

concepts.name: Unhandled rejection diagnosis
concepts.summary: Find forgotten awaits and uncaught rejections and decide on global handling and logging.

concepts.name: Blocking the event loop
concepts.summary: Evaluate CPU-heavy work that starves the loop and choose chunking or Web Workers to offload it.

concepts.name: Debounce and async caching
concepts.summary: Choose debouncing, caching of in-flight promises and deduplication to reduce redundant async work.

misconceptions.text: Web Workers share variables with the main thread, so offloaded work needs no message passing.
Since JavaScript is single-threaded, race conditions cannot occur.
Retrying every failed request immediately is always the safest way to be resilient.

concepts.name: Evaluating async abstractions
concepts.summary: Compare promises, callbacks, event emitters, observables and streams and justify the right fit for a problem.

concepts.name: Designing async architecture
concepts.summary: Design module and API boundaries that expose cancellation, errors, progress and concurrency control consistently.

concepts.name: Building promise utilities
concepts.summary: Implement utilities such as a promise polyfill, task queue or limiter that obey the Promises/A+ semantics.

concepts.name: Structured concurrency patterns
concepts.summary: Create patterns where child async tasks are scoped, cancelled and cleaned up together with their parent.

concepts.name: Runtime differences in scheduling
concepts.summary: Evaluate how browser and Node.js scheduling differ and how that affects ordering and performance.

concepts.name: Testing and observability of async code
concepts.summary: Assess strategies for deterministic async tests, fake timers, tracing and diagnosing flaky timing issues.

concepts.name: Streaming and backpressure
concepts.summary: Evaluate how streaming data with backpressure controls memory and throughput compared with buffering whole results.

misconceptions.text: Promises are always the best abstraction, so streams and observables add nothing for repeated or large data.
Event loop ordering is identical in browsers and Node.js, so scheduling code is portable.
Adding timeouts and retries at every layer of a system makes it more reliable.
